type.description: The message name — <name> in the routing key.

domain.description: The owning domain — <domain> in the routing key.

kind.description: Which exchange carries this message. Never reaches the routing key.

ts.description: The Timer manager's authoritative server timestamp. Every broadcast is an anchor rather than a tick, so a client reconciles its own clock against this before interpolating.

target.description: The timer instance this message addresses — the <target> routing segment. Required on every timer message: a timer is a keyed instance, and 'presentation-phase' is the well-known key of the standing one.

label.description: The cue that fired, matching its label in the timer's cue set.

TimerCueFired.description: A cue was crossed. A crossing is not a transition, so without this nothing would tell a basic display that a cue fired between two anchors — it is the 'furthestCue advanced' push.
